headline: Tonight's last showers fade, leaving Thursday through early Saturday dry and near normal with morning fog, before showers return Sunday and a stronger Tuesday storm brings wind, Cascade pass snow and a coastal flooding risk with next week's peak tides.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: A few showers linger across Western Washington this Wednesday evening as a weakening storm to the south drifts inland, but they should wind down overnight. Winds are mostly light east to northeast at 5 to 10 mph, easing further overnight, with a few gusts near 20 mph around Sea-Tac this evening. Clouds stay high enough that fog should be limited to isolated valleys and low-lying spots tonight.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Thursday turns drier across the Strait shore and the Puget Sound lowlands as the moisture wrapping around the departing storm gets cut off, though a few lingering showers over the southern Cascades can't be ruled out; skies around Seattle should clear by late Thursday morning or afternoon. High pressure building overhead keeps Thursday and Friday quiet, with periods of morning fog and low clouds and cloudy afternoons. Temperatures stay near normal, with lowland highs in the upper 40s to low 50s and lows mostly in the 30s. Near-freezing temperatures early Friday morning could produce pockets of freezing fog in the southwest interior.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Saturday likely stays dry at least through the morning before high pressure shifts east. A slow-moving storm cut off from the main jet stream sets up offshore late Saturday, sending bands of moisture into Western Washington into Sunday with light rain showers in the lowlands, breezy east winds through the Cascade gaps, and snow levels around 2,000 to 2,500 feet giving the mountains a dusting. Monday may bring a brief lull before a stronger, more organized front arrives Tuesday, potentially bringing widespread breezy winds and snow over the Cascade passes. No river flooding is expected over the next 7 days.

coast: Seas of 10 to 13 feet linger in the coastal waters this evening, with a Small Craft Advisory until 10 AM Thursday; seas drop toward 6 to 8 feet during Thursday. High pressure brings calmer conditions on the water Thursday and Friday. It turns active again this weekend into early next week as seas climb back above 10 feet; Monday into Tuesday is the windiest stretch, with gale-force gusts likely in the coastal waters and parts of the Strait of Juan de Fuca, a 40 to 50% chance of storm-force gusts in the outer coastal waters late Monday, and seas approaching 12 to 17 feet by midweek. Astronomical tides peak next week, raising the potential for coastal flooding, which the Tuesday storm's low pressure may make worse.
watch_for: Freezing fog in the southwest interior early Friday morning.
Tuesday's stronger storm: widespread breezy winds and snow over the Cascade passes.
Coastal flooding risk next week as peak high tides coincide with the Tuesday storm.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in a quiet, mostly dry Thursday through Saturday morning; models continue to show Tuesday's system as stronger and more organized, though its exact wind, pass snow and coastal flooding impacts are still uncertain.
